_comment: Heavy-load counterpart to steady_state_l008.json (results/0902d, 0902e) -- same instance, same fixed-duration methodology, only arrivalLambda changed (0.008 -> 0.044, the original 0901 heavy-load rate, ~4-5x measured capacity). Purpose: decision_log.csv from 0902e showed dispatch decisions are degenerate (candidate_count<=1, rule never runs) 92-99% of the time for the 7 non-MMUR rules at slack load -- does raising load toward/above capacity reduce that rate the way naive queueing intuition predicts, or does something else (AGV-transport pacing) keep queues thin regardless? Duration shorter (15000s vs 30000s) since we need decision-log volume, not full flow-time statistics this time -- at lambda=0.044 with dynamicJobCap=0 (unlimited) arrivals will outpace capacity for the WHOLE duration (~660 expected arrivals vs ~150-180 processable), so WIP will grow throughout rather than plateau -- expected and fine for this purpose, NOT comparable to steady_state_l008's steady-state framing. REQUIRES --baselinedrain true.
